chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Mukhallad ibn Musa from Ibrahim ibn Ali from Ali ibn Yahya al-Yarbu'i from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am a human being like you; I marry from among you and give in marriage to you, except Fatimah (peace be upon her), for her marriage descended from the heaven.'
ai.seo_question: What makes the marriage of Fatimah (peace be upon her) unique compared to the Prophet's other marriages?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the unique ontological status of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her) by contrasting the Prophet's ordinary marital choices with the celestial nature of her union. Shia scholars interpret 'descended from the heaven' as indicating that her marriage was not merely a social contract but a divine decree, reinforcing her role as the spiritual and physical continuation of the Prophetic lineage. This distinction underscores the concept of 'Nass' (divine designation) in Shia theology, where key figures are chosen by God rather than selected through human preference.

en.sarwar: 54. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘ Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al- Mukhallad ibn Musa from Ibrahim ibn Ali from Ali ibn Yahya al-Yarbu‘iy from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘I am a human being like you. I marry from you and give in marriage to you except Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, because her marriage came from the heaven.’”
